dominant_strengths: Clean SF typography with disciplined hierarchy between eyebrow, headline, and body across all four cards
Each card image has distinct visual treatment (photo, product render, logo cluster, illustration) showing strong art direction
Card-based horizontal scroll pattern is well-executed with clear affordances via plus and chevron icons
dominant_weaknesses: Footnote markers (*, 1, 12) collide awkwardly with body copy creating typographic noise and ambiguous reference numbers
Visual languages between cards feel inconsistent — flat illustration next to photoreal product breaks the row's rhythm
Truncated rightmost card is a functional cue but reads as cramped rather than inviting at this crop
fix_priorities: Resolve footnote glyph treatment — use superscript styling and consistent numbering to remove visual debris
Unify card imagery treatment (shared lighting, scale, or background) for a more cohesive scroll row
Strengthen the affordance/preview of the partially-visible card to better signal horizontal scroll
rationale.norman_balance: Heavily behavioral (informational, transactional cards) with moderate visceral polish and low reflective payoff beyond commerce utility.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it functions as an Apple.com iPhone marketing scroll module, on-brand and on-pattern, but lacks distinctive innovation.
